    Terror attack · Apr 2025

    Pahalgam terror attack (22 April 2025)

    Terrorists killed 26 tourists, mostly Hindus, in the Baisaran valley near Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir — the deadliest civilian terror attack in India since 26/11. The Resistance Front (TRF), a Lashkar-e-Taiba proxy, claimed responsibility. The attack triggered India's biggest military response to terrorism in decades.

    National · Apr 2025

    CCS response: Indus Waters Treaty held in abeyance

    On 23 April 2025 the Cabinet Committee on Security put the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance, closed the Attari-Wagah border, cancelled SAARC visas for Pakistanis and expelled Pakistani defence advisors. It was the first time the water treaty was suspended. Diplomatic ties were effectively frozen.

    Op Sindoor · May 2025

    Operation Sindoor begins (7 May 2025)

    In the early hours of 7 May 2025 India launched Operation Sindoor, striking nine terror facilities in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, including Jaish-e-Mohammed's Bahawalpur headquarters and Lashkar-e-Taiba's Muridke base. Rafales fired SCALP cruise missiles and Su-30MKIs launched BrahMos missiles from Indian airspace. It was India's deepest strike inside Pakistan since 1971.

    Op Sindoor · May 2025

    Why 'Sindoor'? The codename's meaning

    The government chose the name Operation Sindoor to honour the women widowed in the Pahalgam attack — sindoor being the vermilion worn by married Hindu women. The messaging framed the operation as justice for the victims' families. The codename itself became a national talking point.

    Op Sindoor · May 2025

    Sindoor's arsenal: SCALP, BrahMos, S-400

    Operation Sindoor showcased India's stand-off strike triad: Rafale jets with SCALP cruise missiles, Su-30MKIs with BrahMos, and Mirage-2000s in support roles. When Pakistan retaliated with drones and missiles, the S-400 system and indigenous Akash batteries intercepted them over Punjab and Jammu. The Akashteer air-defence network coordinated the response.

    Op Sindoor · May 2025

    Ceasefire via DGMOs (10 May 2025)

    After four days of strikes and counter-strikes, firing stopped on the evening of 10 May 2025. Then-CDS General Anil Chauhan later confirmed the ceasefire was settled directly between the Indian and Pakistani Directors General of Military Operations, with no third-party mediation. Pakistan's DGMO initiated the hotline call.

    Op Sindoor · May 2025

    Pakistan's Operation Bunyan-un-Marsoos

    On 10 May 2025 Pakistan launched retaliatory strikes under the codename Operation Bunyan-un-Marsoos (Arabic for 'a solid structure'), targeting Indian airbases with its Fatah-series missiles and drones. Indian air defences largely blunted the attack. Hours later, Pakistan sought the DGMO-level ceasefire.

    Op Sindoor · May 2025

    PM's 12 May address: the 'new normal'

    On 12 May 2025 Prime Minister Modi declared that India would no longer tolerate 'nuclear blackmail', and that 'terror and talks cannot go together, terror and trade cannot go together'. He said Operation Sindoor had set a 'new normal' in India's counter-terror doctrine. The speech is now quoted as the Sindoor Doctrine.

    Op Sindoor · 2025

    Western Air Command ran the air war

    Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra, then Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of Western Air Command, directed the air operations of Operation Sindoor from 7–10 May 2025. On Independence Day 2025 President Droupadi Murmu conferred on him the Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal, India's highest wartime distinguished-service decoration.

    Op Sindoor · 2025

    Navy's role: containing Pakistan at sea

    During Operation Sindoor the Navy deployed its carrier battle group in the Arabian Sea in an aggressive posture. Navy Chief Admiral Dinesh K. Tripathi later said swift deployment 'contained' the Pakistan Navy and 'compelled them to seek an end to kinetic actions'. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, aboard INS Vikrant on 30 May 2025, warned the operation was 'not yet over'.

    Op Sindoor · 2025

    Shangri-La: CDS on losses and lessons

    At the Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore (May–June 2025), then-CDS General Anil Chauhan acknowledged that aircraft losses 'are a part of combat', while stressing that tactics were swiftly corrected and objectives met. He later said Pakistan tried using Chinese commercial satellite imagery to track Indian movements. His frankness made global headlines.

    National · Sep 2026

    Sindoor commander to head Ram Mandir Trust

    In September 2026 the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust named retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra — the officer who commanded the Western Air Command during Operation Sindoor — as the first Chief Executive Officer of the Ayodhya Ram temple. He had retired from the IAF in April 2026.

    Defence · 2026

    Forces ready for 'Sindoor 2.0' if needed

    In mid-2026 the Army leadership said the armed forces remained prepared for another round of Operation Sindoor if Pakistan-sponsored terrorism resurfaced. The statement underlined that the post-Pahalgam doctrine of punitive retaliation remains active policy.

    Awards · Aug 2025

    Operation Sindoor gallantry honours

    The 2025 Independence Day gallantry list recognised Operation Sindoor's commanders, led by the Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal for Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra. Only ten officers had received the SYSM since its institution in 1980. Unit citations also went to air-defence and strike formations.

    Leadership · May 2026

    India's third CDS: General N. S. Raja Subramani

    General N. S. Raja Subramani, former Vice Chief of the Army Staff, took over as India's third Chief of Defence Staff on 31 May 2026, succeeding General Anil Chauhan. He inherits the long-pending theatre-command reforms. His first task: presenting the final theatreisation blueprint to the Defence Minister.

    Reforms · 2026

    Theatre commands: final blueprint ready

    Before stepping down on 30 May 2026, CDS General Anil Chauhan completed the final blueprint for reorganising the forces into integrated theatre commands — a reform debated for nearly two decades. New CDS Subramani is expected to take the plan to Defence Minister Rajnath Singh for the most profound military restructuring since Independence.

    Leadership · Jun 2026

    31st Army Chief: General Dhiraj Seth

    General Dhiraj Seth took over as the 31st Chief of the Army Staff on 30 June 2026 from General Upendra Dwivedi. An Armoured Corps officer commissioned in December 1986, he is the first armoured-corps chief since General Shankar Roy Chowdhury (1997). He earlier commanded both the South Western and Southern Commands.

    Leadership · Jun 2026

    General Upendra Dwivedi's tenure ends

    General Upendra Dwivedi retired on 30 June 2026 after two years as the 30th Army Chief. His tenure covered Operation Sindoor, the 'Decade of Transformation' reforms, and new tech formations like Rudra Brigades and drone platoons. He championed the 'Eagle on the Arm' vision of drone-training every soldier.

    Leadership · 2026

    Service chiefs hold steady in 2026

    Mid-2026 brought a change of guard at the top: Vice Admiral Krishna Swaminathan took over as the 27th Chief of the Naval Staff on 31 May 2026, succeeding Admiral Dinesh K. Tripathi (CNS since April 2024). The other service chiefs held steady: Air Chief Marshal A. P. Singh (CAS since September 2024) and — from 30 June 2026 — General Dhiraj Seth as COAS. Continuity at the top aided the post-Sindoor modernisation push.

    Leadership · 2025-26

    Rajnath Singh: continuity at South Block

    Rajnath Singh continued as Defence Minister through 2025–26, overseeing Operation Sindoor, record defence exports and the biggest indigenous procurement deals in a decade. He presided over the MiG-21 farewell (September 2025) and the INS Udaygiri–Himgiri commissioning (August 2025).

    Op Sindoor · May 2025

    Defence Minister's 'not yet over' warning

    Addressing sailors aboard INS Vikrant on 30 May 2025, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said Operation Sindoor was 'not just a military action' and had not concluded — the Navy could be called upon again. The remark, days after the ceasefire, signalled sustained coercive posture against Pakistan.

    Defence expo · Feb 2025

    Aero India 2025 (Bengaluru)

    The 15th Aero India was held at Yelahanka, Bengaluru from 10–14 February 2025 with the theme 'The Runway to a Billion Opportunities'. It drew record business and foreign participation, with the indigenous AMCA, Tejas Mk1A and Prachand in the spotlight. Defence ministers' conclave and iDEX start-up pavilions anchored the Atmanirbhar pitch.

    Reforms · 2025

    2025: the 'Year of Reforms'

    The Defence Ministry declared 2025 the 'Year of Reforms', targeting jointness, theatre commands, faster procurement and technology absorption. The Rudra Brigades, Bhairav Battalions and integrated battle groups rolled out under this banner. Operation Sindoor became its first real-world test.

    Budget · Feb 2025

    Defence budget 2025–26: ₹6.81 lakh crore

    The Union Budget allocated ₹6.81 lakh crore to defence for 2025–26 — the highest ever, about 13% of central expenditure. Capital outlay for modernisation crossed ₹1.8 lakh crore, with a record share earmarked for domestic industry. The allocation underwrote the Rafale-Marine, Prachand and ATAGS deals.

    Exports · 2025

    Defence exports hit record ₹23,622 crore

    India's defence exports touched a record ₹23,622 crore in FY 2024–25, up from ₹21,083 crore the year before, with BrahMos, Pinaka, radars and patrol vessels leading. The government targets ₹50,000 crore in exports by 2029. DPSUs and private firms both contributed to the surge.

    Deal · Apr 2025

    Rafale-Marine deal signed (April 2025)

    On 28 April 2025 India signed a ~₹63,000-crore inter-governmental deal with France for 26 Rafale-Marine fighters (22 single-seat, 4 twin-seat) for the Navy's carriers. Deliveries begin around 2028, with India-specific enhancements. It is the biggest naval aviation deal in Indian history.

    Deal · Mar 2025

    156 Prachand helicopters ordered (March 2025)

    In March 2025 the Defence Ministry signed a ~₹62,700-crore contract with HAL for 156 Light Combat Helicopters 'Prachand' — 90 for the IAF and 66 for the Army. It is the largest helicopter order in Indian history. The LCH is the only attack helicopter designed for high-altitude warfare.

    Deal · Mar 2025

    307 ATAGS guns ordered (March 2025)

    The Cabinet Committee on Security cleared the ₹7,000-crore purchase of 307 Advanced Towed Artillery Gun Systems (155mm/52 calibre) in March 2025, split between Tata Advanced Systems and Bharat Forge. ATAGS, with a 48-km range, is the DRDO-designed gun meant to replace ageing Bofors-era artillery.

    Deal · Oct 2024

    MQ-9B Predator deal (October 2024)

    On 15 October 2024 India signed a $3.48-billion deal with the US for 31 MQ-9B Predator drones — 15 SeaGuardians for the Navy and 16 SkyGuardians split between the Army and IAF. The high-altitude, long-endurance drones will transform surveillance over the Indian Ocean and the northern borders.

    Navy · Jan 2025

    Triple commissioning: Nilgiri, Surat, Vagsheer (Jan 2025)

    On 15 January 2025 Prime Minister Modi commissioned three frontline platforms together at Mumbai: the P15B destroyer INS Surat, the lead P17A stealth frigate INS Nilgiri, and the sixth Scorpene submarine INS Vagsheer. The triple induction — a destroyer, frigate and submarine in one day — was a first for the Navy.

    Navy · Dec 2024

    INS Tushil commissioned in Russia (Dec 2024)

    INS Tushil, the first of two Talwar-class follow-on frigates built at Russia's Yantar Shipyard, was commissioned on 9 December 2024 in the presence of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. It carries BrahMos missiles and 26% indigenous content. Its sister ship INS Tamal followed in July 2025.

    Navy · Jul 2025

    INS Tamal: last foreign-built warship (Jul 2025)

    INS Tamal (F71) was commissioned on 1 July 2025 at Kaliningrad, Russia — the eighth Talwar-class frigate and, officially, the last major warship India will induct from abroad. Named after the mythical sword of Lord Indra, she joins the Western Fleet at Karwar with BrahMos missiles and HUMSA-NG sonar.

    Navy · Jul 2025

    INS Nistar: indigenous diving support vessel (Jul 2025)

    INS Nistar, India's first indigenously designed and built diving support vessel, was commissioned on 18 July 2025 at Visakhapatnam. Built by Hindustan Shipyard, she supports deep-sea diving and submarine rescue operations. Her induction fills a critical gap in submarine rescue capability.

    Navy · Aug 2025

    Udaygiri + Himgiri: historic double commissioning (Aug 2025)

    On 26 August 2025 the Navy commissioned INS Udaygiri and INS Himgiri together at Visakhapatnam — the first simultaneous commissioning of two warships built at different shipyards (MDL Mumbai and GRSE Kolkata). Both P17A stealth frigates carry 75% indigenous content and BrahMos missiles.

    IAF · Sep 2025

    MiG-21 farewell after 62 years (Sep 2025)

    On 26 September 2025 the IAF bid farewell to the MiG-21 at Chandigarh, ending 62 years of service for India's first supersonic fighter. Air Chief Marshal A. P. Singh flew the final sortie of No. 23 Squadron 'Panthers'. Over 870 MiG-21s served the IAF across the 1965, 1971 and Kargil wars and the Balakot strike.

    Army · Jul 2025

    Army's first Apaches arrive (Jul 2025)

    The first three of six AH-64E Apache attack helicopters for the Indian Army arrived at Hindon on 22 July 2025, ending a long-delayed delivery. Based at Jodhpur, they give Army Aviation its first dedicated tank-killer helicopter for the western front. The remaining three followed in phases.

    Navy · Apr 2026

    INS Taragiri joins the fleet (Apr 2026)

    Defence Minister Rajnath Singh commissioned the stealth frigate INS Taragiri — the fourth Project 17A vessel — at Visakhapatnam in April 2026. Built by Mazagon Dock with over 75% indigenous content, she carries BrahMos and Barak-8 missiles. Sister ship INS Mahendragiri is expected later in 2026 (reported).

    Navy · Jun 2026

    INS Dunagiri commissioned (Jun 2026)

    The Navy commissioned the stealth frigate INS Dunagiri — the fifth Project 17A (Nilgiri-class) warship — at Kolkata in June 2026. At ~149 metres and 6,600 tonnes, she is among India's most advanced surface combatants, with BrahMos, Barak-8 and MF-STAR radar. Two more P17A frigates are due within months.

    Navy · 2026

    19 new ships for the Navy in 2026

    The Navy planned to add 19 ships in 2026 as indigenous construction peaked, including Project 17A frigates, survey vessels and support ships. The surge reflects the 'Aatmanirbhar' shipbuilding pipeline at MDL, GRSE, GSL and CSL. Commissionings like Dunagiri and Taragiri are part of this wave.

    Navy · Sep 2026

    NGMV keel laid at Kochi (Sep 2026)

    On 18 September 2026 Cochin Shipyard laid the keel of the first of six Next Generation Missile Vessels for the Navy. The high-speed (33-knot) vessels will carry surface-to-surface missiles, anti-missile defences and advanced radars. The ₹9,804-crore contract was signed in March 2023; first delivery is due March 2027.

    IAF · 2026 · reported

    First India-made C-295 rolls out (2026)

    The first C-295 transport aircraft assembled in India was slated to roll out of the Tata-Airbus facility at Vadodara in September 2026, under the ₹21,935-crore deal for 56 aircraft. Sixteen were delivered fly-away from Spain; the remaining 40 are being built in India through 2031, replacing the ageing Avro fleet.

    IAF · 2025

    97 more Tejas Mk1A cleared (2023); deliveries begin

    The Defence Acquisition Council cleared 97 additional Tejas Mk1A fighters in November 2023, taking the total order past 180. After delays over GE F404 engine supplies, deliveries of the Mk1A began in 2025. The indigenous fighter is the IAF's answer to its depleting squadron strength.

    Navy · 2026 · reported

    Third SSBN Aridaman expected 2026

    INS Aridaman, India's third Arihant-class nuclear ballistic-missile submarine, was expected to join the fleet in 2026, with a fourth SSBN (S-4*) to follow in 2027 (reported). Together with INS Arihant and INS Arighaat, Aridaman will cement the sea leg of India's nuclear triad.

    Navy · 2025 · reported

    Project 75I: six submarines in negotiation

    India advanced negotiations through 2025 for Project 75I — six advanced diesel-electric submarines to be built at Mazagon Dock with Germany's ThyssenKrupp Marine Systems as technology partner (reported). The deal, among the costliest 'Make in India' projects, will add air-independent propulsion submarines to the fleet.

    Army · 2024 · reported

    K9 Vajra: 100 more guns cleared (reported)

    The Cabinet Committee on Security reportedly cleared the purchase of 100 additional K9 Vajra-T self-propelled howitzers in late 2024, doubling the Army's fleet of the L&T-built 155mm/52 guns. The repeat order validated the gun's performance in Ladakh's high-altitude deserts.

    Navy · Feb 2024

    INS Sandhayak: new survey ship (Feb 2024)

    INS Sandhayak, the lead vessel of the new Sandhayak-class survey ships, was commissioned on 3 February 2024 at Visakhapatnam. Built by GRSE, she maps the oceans for navigational charts — dual-use work that underpins both naval operations and blue-economy planning.

    Missiles · Mar 2024

    Mission Divyastra: Agni-5 with MIRV (Mar 2024)

    On 11 March 2024 DRDO tested Agni-5 with Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle (MIRV) technology under 'Mission Divyastra'. The test put India in the elite club of nations with MIRV capability, alongside the US, Russia, China, France and the UK. Range: over 5,000 km.

    Missiles · Nov 2024

    Hypersonic LRAShM tested (Nov 2024)

    In November 2024 DRDO flight-tested the Long Range Anti-Ship Missile (LRAShM), a hypersonic missile with a 1,500-km range, from the Integrated Test Range. The test marked India's entry into the hypersonic-weapons club. The missile is designed to strike warships far out at sea.

    Missiles · Nov 2024

    LRLACM maiden test (Nov 2024)

    On 12 November 2024 DRDO conducted the maiden flight-test of the Long Range Land Attack Cruise Missile (LRLACM) from Chandipur, Odisha. The 1,000-km-class subsonic cruise missile is the successor to Nirbhay, with improved manoeuvrability and indigenous propulsion.

    Missiles · Nov 2024

    K-4 SLBM fired from INS Arighaat (Nov 2024)

    In November 2024 India test-fired the 3,500-km-range K-4 submarine-launched ballistic missile from the newly commissioned INS Arighaat. The test validated the sea leg of the nuclear triad beyond the 750-km K-15. A longer-range K-5/K-6 family is under development (reported).

    Missiles · May 2024

    Rudram-II tested (May 2024)

    In May 2024 the IAF successfully flight-tested the Rudram-II air-to-surface missile from a Su-30MKI off the Odisha coast. The solid-propelled missile can strike enemy radars and communication nodes at long range. Rudram-1, its predecessor, was tested in 2020.

    Missiles · Aug 2025

    Agni-5 test-fired again (Aug 2025)

    On 20 August 2025 India test-fired the Agni-5 intermediate-range ballistic missile from Chandipur, with DRDO stating all operational and technical parameters were validated. The test, months after Operation Sindoor, reaffirmed the credibility of the land leg of the nuclear triad.

    Missiles · Sep 2024

    VL-SRSAM tested (Sep 2024)

    In September 2024 DRDO and the Navy successfully flight-tested the Vertical Launch Short Range Surface-to-Air Missile (VL-SRSAM) from Chandipur. The indigenous system will replace ageing foreign short-range missiles on frontline warships, giving them a 360-degree air-defence shield.

    Air defence · Aug 2025

    Mission Sudarshan Chakra announced (Aug 2025)

    On Independence Day 2025 the Prime Minister announced 'Mission Sudarshan Chakra' — a plan for an expanded, multi-layered national air-defence shield within ten years, integrating radars, interceptors and space-based sensors. The announcement drew directly on Operation Sindoor's air-defence successes.

    Missiles · 2025 · reported

    MPATGM completes trials (reported 2025)

    The Man-Portable Anti-Tank Guided Missile (MPATGM), DRDO's fire-and-forget infantry missile, completed its final user trials in 2025 (reported), clearing the way for Army induction. It gives infantry a lightweight answer to enemy armour without laser designation.

    Exports · 2025 · reported

    BrahMos export push: Indonesia talks (reported)

    After the Philippines received its first BrahMos battery in April 2024, Indonesia emerged in 2025 as the next likely buyer, with advanced price negotiations reported. Vietnam and other Southeast Asian nations have also shown interest. BrahMos Aerospace targets $5 billion in exports by 2026.

    Op Sindoor · May 2025

    Akash proves itself in combat

    During Operation Sindoor (May 2025) the indigenous Akash surface-to-air missile system intercepted Pakistani drones and missiles over Punjab and Jammu, its first combat debut. The performance boosted export interest, with Armenia already a buyer and more nations in talks (reported).

    Exports · 2024-25 · reported

    Pinaka's export run: Armenia deliveries

    Deliveries of the Pinaka multi-barrel rocket system to Armenia, ordered in 2022, proceeded through 2024–25 (reported) — India's biggest artillery export. The deal, worth about $250 million, marked the system's evolution from Kargil-war workhorse to export product.

    Exercise · 2024

    Tarang Shakti: India's first multinational air exercise (2024)

    From August to September 2024 the IAF hosted Tarang Shakti, India's first multinational air exercise, in two phases at Sulur and Jodhpur. Air forces from the US, France, Germany, Australia, Japan and others flew alongside Rafales, Su-30MKIs and Tejas. It announced India as a convenor of air power in the Indo-Pacific.

    Exercise · Feb 2024

    Milan 2024: 50+ navies at Visakhapatnam

    The 12th edition of the Milan multilateral naval exercise was held off Visakhapatnam in February 2024 with over 50 navies participating — the largest ever. The harbour and sea phases included anti-submarine and air-defence drills. Milan anchors India's naval diplomacy in the Indo-Pacific.

    Exercise · Oct 2024

    Malabar 2024 off Visakhapatnam

    The 28th Malabar naval exercise, with the Quad navies of India, the US, Japan and Australia, was held off Visakhapatnam in October 2024. Complex anti-submarine and air-defence serials sharpened interoperability. Malabar began as a bilateral India-US exercise in 1992.

    Exercise · Sep 2024

    Yudh Abhyas 2024 (Rajasthan)

    The 20th India-US joint military exercise Yudh Abhyas was held in Rajasthan in September 2024, focusing on counter-terrorism and UN peacekeeping scenarios in semi-desert terrain. The annual exercise is the largest bilateral Army drill India conducts.

    Exercise · Nov 2024

    Poorvi Prahar: tri-service drill in Arunachal (Nov 2024)

    In November 2024 the armed forces conducted 'Poorvi Prahar', a tri-service exercise in Arunachal Pradesh testing joint operations against the China front. Army, Navy and Air Force assets practised integrated surveillance, strike and logistics in high-altitude terrain — a template for theatre commands.

    Exercise · Jan 2025

    Desert Knight: India-France-UAE air drill (Jan 2025)

    In January 2025 the air forces of India, France and the UAE held 'Desert Knight' over the Arabian Sea — a trilateral combat exercise with Su-30MKIs, Rafales, Mirage-2000s and F-16s. The drill built on the bilateral air cooperation deepened since the Rafale inductions.

    Exercise · Jan 2025

    La Perouse 2025: INS Mumbai with France

    In January 2025 the destroyer INS Mumbai participated in the French-led multilateral exercise La Perouse in the Indian Ocean, alongside French, American, British, Australian and other warships. The exercise practises maritime interdiction and cooperation under French command in the Indo-Pacific.

    Exercise · Feb-Mar 2025

    Dharma Guardian 2025 (Japan)

    The 6th India-Japan Army exercise Dharma Guardian was held in Japan from February to March 2025, focusing on counter-terrorism in urban and semi-urban terrain. The annual drill reflects the deepening India-Japan security partnership under their special strategic partnership.

    Exercise · Feb 2025

    Ekuverin 2025 (Maldives)

    The 13th India-Maldives joint exercise Ekuverin was held in the Maldives in February 2025, centred on counter-insurgency and counter-terrorism. The drill continued despite the 2023–24 diplomatic chill, signalling the reset in defence ties after President Muizzu's October 2024 India visit.

    Exercise · Mar 2025

    Varuna 2025 with French carrier group

    The 23rd India-France naval exercise Varuna was held in March 2025 in the Arabian Sea, with the French carrier Charles de Gaulle's strike group exercising alongside INS Vikrant, destroyers and submarines. Anti-submarine warfare and carrier operations were the focus — the most complex Varuna yet.

    Exercise · Apr 2025

    Tiger Triumph 2025: tri-service amphibious drill

    The fourth India-US tri-service amphibious exercise Tiger Triumph was held off Visakhapatnam and Kakinada in April 2025. Army, Navy and Air Force elements practised amphibious landings and HADR operations. The drill is the flagship of India-US jointness.

    Exercise · Jun-Jul 2025

    Shakti 2025 (France)

    The 8th India-France Army exercise Shakti was held at La Cavalerie, France from June to July 2025, with Indian troops training in European terrain and combined-arms tactics. The biennial exercise alternates between India and France and builds interoperability for coalition operations.

    Exercise · 2025

    Khaan Quest 2025 (Mongolia)

    An Indian Army contingent participated in the multinational peacekeeping exercise Khaan Quest 2025 in Mongolia (June–July 2025), alongside US and regional forces. The exercise practises UN-mandate peacekeeping tasks — a domain where India is among the world's largest contributors.

    Exercise · 2025

    Nomadic Elephant 2025 (Mongolia)

    The 17th India-Mongolia joint exercise Nomadic Elephant was held in Mongolia in 2025, focused on counter-terrorism in semi-urban terrain. The long-running drill is a pillar of India's defence engagement with Central Asia.

    Exercise · Nov 2024

    Garuda Shakti 2024 (Indonesia)

    The 9th India-Indonesia special forces exercise Garuda Shakti was held in Indonesia in November 2024, with Para (SF) troops training in jungle warfare and counter-terrorism. Special-forces drills like this build interoperability for regional contingencies.

    Exercise · Nov 2024

    Vajra Prahar 2024 (US)

    The 15th India-US special forces exercise Vajra Prahar was held at Boise, Idaho in November 2024. Para (SF) and US Green Berets trained in joint special operations, airborne insertion and combat shooting. The drill alternates between India and the US.

    Exercise · Jan 2025

    Sea Dragon 2025 (Guam)

    The Indian Navy's P-8I long-range maritime patrol aircraft participated in the multinational anti-submarine exercise Sea Dragon 2025 off Guam in January 2025, alongside the US, Japan, Australia and South Korea. The P-8I is the Navy's primary sub-hunter in the Indian Ocean.

    Exercise · Jan 2025 · reported

    TARKASH 2025: NSG–US drill (reported)

    The 8th India-US joint counter-terror exercise TARKASH was reportedly held in Kolkata in January 2025, with the NSG training alongside US special forces in urban intervention and chemical-biological scenarios. The drill sharpens responses to 26/11-style attacks.

    Exercise · Sep 2026

    Varuna 2026: INS Trishul at Toulon

    In September 2026 the frigate INS Trishul arrived at Toulon, France for the bilateral naval exercise Varuna, sporting new BrahMos-capable launchers and Indian sensors. The deployment underlined the upgraded Talwar-class fleet's role in Indo-Pacific cooperation with France.

    Exercise · Mar 2025

    Khanjar 2025 (Kyrgyzstan)

    The 12th India-Kyrgyzstan special forces exercise Khanjar was held in Kyrgyzstan in March 2025, focused on counter-terrorism in mountainous terrain. The annual drill sustains India's Central Asian defence partnerships.

    Exercise · Feb 2025

    Cyclone 2025: India-Egypt drill

    The 3rd India-Egypt joint exercise Cyclone was held in Rajasthan in February 2025, with special forces of both countries training in desert counter-terrorism. Defence ties with Egypt have grown steadily since 2022.

    Exercise · Oct 2024

    Naseem Al Bahr 2024 (Oman)

    The India-Oman bilateral naval exercise Naseem Al Bahr was held off Goa in October 2024, covering anti-air, anti-surface and VBSS operations. Oman is India's oldest defence partner in the Gulf, hosting Indian naval access at Duqm port.

    Exercise · Jan-Mar 2025

    TROPEX 2025: Navy's mega theatre drill

    The Navy's biennial Theatre Level Operational Readiness Exercise (TROPEX-25) was conducted from January to March 2025 across the Indian Ocean, involving 65+ ships, submarines and aircraft of all three services. It validated joint operational concepts ahead of the theatre-command reforms.

    Navy · Apr 2025

    IOS Sagar: Indian Ocean outreach (Apr 2025)

    On 5 April 2025 the offshore patrol vessel INS Sunayna sailed from Karwar on the maiden 'Indian Ocean Ship SAGAR' mission, carrying 44 naval personnel from nine Indian Ocean nations. The initiative trains partner navies and extends the SAGAR doctrine into a cooperative maritime-security framework.

    National · Mar 2025

    MAHASAGAR vision unveiled (Mar 2025)

    During his March 2025 Mauritius visit the Prime Minister unveiled 'MAHASAGAR' — Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions — expanding the 2015 SAGAR doctrine. The vision bundles trade, capacity-building and maritime security for the Global South.

    Reforms · 2025

    Rudra Brigades: the Army's new fists

    In 2025 the Army began raising 'Rudra' all-arms brigades — integrated formations combining infantry, mechanised forces, artillery, air defence and drones under one commander. The concept, part of the Decade of Transformation, was battle-validated during Operation Sindoor.

    Reforms · 2025

    Bhairav battalions, Ashni platoons, Shaktibaan regiments

    Alongside Rudra Brigades, the Army raised Bhairav light-commando battalions, Ashni drone platoons, Shaktibaan artillery regiments and Divyastra batteries in 2025. The new units embed drones, electronic warfare and long-range fires down to battalion level.

    Reforms · 2025

    Decade of Transformation (2023–2032)

    The Army's 'Decade of Transformation' roadmap (2023–2032) drives force restructuring, technology absorption and human-resource reforms. Operation Sindoor became its first major validation, with networked air defence, drones and precision fires deciding the short, sharp campaign.

    Air defence · 2024-25

    Akashteer: battle-tested air-defence network

    The Army's indigenous Akashteer air-defence control and reporting system, inducted from 2024, networked radars and guns during Operation Sindoor to defeat Pakistani drones and missiles. Its combat debut made it the poster child of Atmanirbhar air defence.

    Army · 2025 · reported

    Project Sanjay: battlefield surveillance (reported)

    The Army's 'Sanjay' battlefield surveillance system — integrating sensors, drones and satellites into a common operational picture — was reported inducted in 2025. It promises commanders a real-time digital map of the battlefield down to brigade level.

    Army · 2024-25

    Zorawar light tank trials in Ladakh

    The DRDO–L&T Zorawar light tank underwent high-altitude trials in Ladakh through 2024–25, including firing trials in desert and mountain terrain. Designed for the China front, the 25-tonne tank answers the PLA's light-tank deployments across the LAC.

    Agniveer · 2026 · reported

    Agniveer: first batch completes four years (2026)

    The first Agniveer batch, recruited in 2022 under the Agnipath scheme, completes its four-year engagement in 2026 — when the scheme's 25%-retention rule faces its first real test. Over a lakh Agniveers have joined the forces since 2022 (reported). The 2026 retention round will shape the scheme's future.

    Agniveer · 2022-25

    Women Agniveers in the Navy

    The Navy inducted its first women Agniveers in 2022–23, posting them across branches including as sailors on frontline warships. The move, part of the Agnipath scheme, opened sea-going roles that were long restricted. Women now serve on destroyers and fleet tankers.

    NDA · May 2025

    NDA's first women cadets pass out (May 2025)

    On 30 May 2025 seventeen women cadets of the NDA's 154th course passed out at Khadakwasla — the first women to graduate from the tri-service academy. They had joined in 2021 after the Supreme Court opened NDA entry to women. The moment was hailed as a milestone for military gender integration.

    Army · Oct 2024

    Territorial Army's 75th Raising Day (Oct 2024)

    The Territorial Army celebrated its 75th Raising Day on 9 October 2024. The citizen-soldiers' force, raised in 1949, contributes infantry battalions, ecological units and railway engineers to national service. Its motto spirit: part-time soldiers, full-time commitment.

    Reforms · 2024

    Fifth indigenisation list: 509 items embargoed

    By 2024 the Defence Ministry had issued five 'positive indigenisation lists' embargoing 509 weapons, systems and components from import on staggered timelines. The lists force the services to buy Indian — from artillery guns to aero-engines — and anchor the Atmanirbhar defence economy.

    IAF · Mar 2024

    AMCA prototype cleared (Mar 2024)

    On 7 March 2024 the Cabinet Committee on Security approved ~₹15,000 crore for prototype development of the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA), India's fifth-generation stealth fighter. ADA and HAL will build five prototypes, with first flight targeted around 2028 (reported).

    HADR · Mar 2025

    Operation Brahma: Myanmar earthquake relief (2025)

    After the devastating March 2025 earthquake in Myanmar, India launched Operation Brahma — IAF C-130Js and C-17s airlifted rescue teams, field hospitals and relief material to Mandalay, while Navy ships carried aid. The HADR mission reinforced India's 'first responder' role in the region.

    LAC · Oct 2024

    LAC breakthrough: Depsang–Demchok pact (Oct 2024)

    In October 2024 India and China reached a patrolling agreement for Depsang and Demchok in eastern Ladakh, ending the four-year stand-off that began at Galwan in 2020. Disengagement was completed and patrolling resumed — the biggest thaw on the LAC since the clash.

    LAC · 2024

    Eastern Ladakh: patrolling resumes

    Following the October 2024 agreement, Indian and Chinese troops resumed coordinated patrolling in Depsang and Demchok by late 2024. The Army maintained its Operation Snow Leopard deployment posture even as buffer zones were negotiated at remaining friction points.

    Army · 2026

    'Eagle on the Arm': drone for every soldier

    Outgoing Army Chief General Upendra Dwivedi's parting vision — 'Eagle on the Arm' — aims to train every soldier as a drone operator, with expanded simulation and training infrastructure. The concept grew from drone lessons of Operation Sindoor and the Ukraine war.

    Awards · Aug 2025

    Ashok Chakra for Shubhanshu Shukla (2025)

    On Independence Day 2025 Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla received the Ashok Chakra — India's highest peacetime gallantry award — for piloting the Axiom-4 mission to the International Space Station in June 2025. He became the first Indian to visit the ISS and only the second Indian in space after Rakesh Sharma.

    Space · Jun 2025

    Axiom-4: Indian returns to space (Jun 2025)

    On 25 June 2025 IAF Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla flew to the International Space Station as pilot of the Axiom-4 commercial mission, 41 years after Rakesh Sharma's 1984 flight. He conducted ISRO-designed experiments aboard the ISS during the 18-day mission.

    National · Jan 2025

    Republic Day 2025: Indonesia chief guest

    India celebrated its 76th Republic Day on 26 January 2025 with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto as chief guest. The parade's theme 'Swarnim Bharat: Virasat aur Vikas' showcased military heritage and self-reliance, with a tri-service tableau and the newly inducted indigenous systems on Rajpath.

    Army · Jan 2025

    Army Day 2025 at Pune

    The 77th Army Day parade was held in Pune on 15 January 2025, continuing the rotation of the parade outside Delhi (Bengaluru 2023, Lucknow 2024). The parade honoured the 1949 takeover by General K. M. Cariappa as the first Indian Army chief.

    Army · Jul 2025

    Kargil Vijay Diwas: 26th anniversary (2025)

    On 26 July 2025 India marked the 26th Kargil Vijay Diwas, honouring the 1999 victory in which 527 soldiers made the supreme sacrifice. Commemorations at the Drass war memorial recalled Operation Vijay's recapture of Tiger Hill and Tololing.

    Army · Dec 2024

    Vijay Diwas: 53rd anniversary (2024)

    On 16 December 2024 India observed the 53rd Vijay Diwas, marking the 1971 surrender of 93,000 Pakistani troops at Dhaka. The Eastern Command's commemorations recalled the 13-day war that created Bangladesh.

    Navy · Dec 2024

    Navy Day 2024 at Puri

    Navy Day 2024 was celebrated at Puri, Odisha on 4 December with a spectacular operational demonstration — ships, submarines, aircraft and Marcos commandos in action off the coast. The Navy has rotated its Day celebrations to coastal cities to connect with the public.

    IAF · Oct 2024

    Air Force Day 2024 at Chennai

    The 92nd Air Force Day parade was held at Chennai's Marina Beach on 8 October 2024, with a massive flypast over the Bay of Bengal. The IAF used the occasion to display Rafales, Tejas, Apaches and the S-400 system to lakhs of spectators.

    Defence · 2024

    First women medical chiefs (2024)

    In 2024 the armed forces got their first women medical chiefs: Lieutenant General Sadhna Saxena Nair became Director General of Medical Services (Army) in August, and Vice Admiral Arti Sarin became Director General of the Armed Forces Medical Services in October. Both were landmark firsts.

    IAF · Oct 2024

    C-295 plant inaugurated at Vadodara (Oct 2024)

    On 28 October 2024 Prime Minister Modi and Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez inaugurated the Tata-Airbus C-295 final assembly line at Vadodara — India's first private military-aircraft plant. The ₹21,935-crore project will build 40 of the 56 ordered transport aircraft in India.

    IAF · Mar 2024

    Tejas Mk1A's first flight (Mar 2024)

    The first production Tejas Mk1A flew in March 2024 from HAL's Nashik facility, beginning the delivery run for the 83-aircraft 2021 order. The Mk1A adds an AESA radar, electronic warfare suite and mid-air refuelling to the indigenous fighter.

    Reforms · Aug 2025 · reported

    Ran Samwad 2025 at Mhow (reported)

    The tri-service seminar 'Ran Samwad 2025' was reportedly held at the Army War College, Mhow in August 2025, with the CDS leading discussions on technology's impact on warfare. The dialogue feeds directly into the theatre-command and joint-doctrine reforms.

    Air defence · 2025 · reported

    S-400: three regiments in service (reported)

    Three of the five S-400 Triumf regiments ordered from Russia in 2018 were delivered by 2023; the remaining two were delayed by the Ukraine war (reported). The deployed systems proved their worth intercepting Pakistani missiles during Operation Sindoor in May 2025.

    IAF · 2026 · reported

    'The Last Salute': MiG-21 documentary (2026)

    The documentary 'The Last Salute', chronicling the MiG-21's 62-year IAF journey, released in August 2026 (reported), featuring Air Chief Marshal A. P. Singh and generations of MiG-21 pilots. The film closed with the emotional September 2025 farewell at Chandigarh.

    Defence GK

    NCC: world's largest uniformed youth body

    The National Cadet Corps, raised under the NCC Act of 1948, remains the world's largest uniformed youth organisation with over 13 lakh cadets. Its motto 'Unity and Discipline' anchors the pipeline that feeds many future officers — NCC 'C' certificate holders get SSB advantages.

    Reforms · 2025 · reported

    Defence Cyber and Space Agencies operationalise

    The Defence Cyber Agency and Defence Space Agency, raised in 2019 under the IDS, steadily operationalised through 2024–25 with dedicated cyber and space warfare cadres. Operation Sindoor saw their first high-tempo employment in networked operations (reported).

    Reforms · 2025 · reported

    iDEX: start-ups enter the arsenal

    By 2025 the Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX) ecosystem had signed 300+ contracts with start-ups and MSMEs under challenges like ADITI and DISC. Drones, AI-based surveillance and loitering munitions from iDEX winners featured in Operation Sindoor's toolkit (reported).

    Exercise · 2025 · reported

    Bongosagar 2025: India-Bangladesh naval drill (reported)

    The bilateral naval exercise Bongosagar between India and Bangladesh was reportedly held in 2025, covering coordinated patrolling and anti-piracy drills in the Bay of Bengal. The drill continued the maritime partnership despite political turbulence in Dhaka.

    Exercise · Dec 2024

    SLINEX 2024: India-Sri Lanka naval exercise

    The bilateral naval exercise SLINEX was held off Visakhapatnam in December 2024, with Sri Lankan warships training alongside the Eastern Fleet. The annual drill covers anti-submarine warfare, gunnery and VBSS — sustaining ties after Sri Lanka's economic crisis years.

    Exercise · 2025 · reported

    Dustlik 2025: India-Uzbekistan drill (reported)

    The 6th India-Uzbekistan joint exercise Dustlik was reportedly held in 2025, focused on counter-terrorism in mountainous and semi-urban terrain. The drill is India's principal Army engagement in Central Asia.

    Exercise · Sep 2024

    Al Najah 2024: India-Oman Army drill

    The 5th India-Oman Army exercise Al Najah was held in Oman in September 2024, centred on desert counter-terrorism operations. Oman hosts Indian listening and berthing facilities at Duqm, making it a key Gulf defence partner.

    Exercise · Dec 2024

    Harimau Shakti 2024: India-Malaysia drill

    The India-Malaysia joint exercise Harimau Shakti was held in Malaysia in December 2024, focused on jungle-warfare counter-terrorism. The drill deepens defence ties under India's Act East policy.

    Exercise · Nov 2024

    Vinbax 2024: India-Vietnam Army drill

    The 5th India-Vietnam bilateral Army exercise Vinbax was held in India in November 2024, with a first-ever inclusion of personnel from both armies' medical and engineering arms. Vietnam is a key BrahMos prospect and strategic partner.

    Exercise · 2024

    Mitra Shakti 2024: India-Sri Lanka Army drill

    The 10th India-Sri Lanka Army exercise Mitra Shakti was held in Sri Lanka in 2024, focused on counter-insurgency in semi-urban terrain. The long-running drill survived the post-civil-war sensitivities to become a model bilateral exercise.

    Exercise · Dec 2024

    Agni Warrior 2024: India-Singapore artillery drill

    The 13th India-Singapore artillery exercise Agni Warrior was held at Deolali in November–December 2024, with Singapore's guns firing alongside Indian artillery. The School of Artillery at Deolali hosts the bilateral live-firing regularly.

    Exercise · 2025 · reported

    Bold Kurukshetra 2025: India-Singapore armour drill (reported)

    The bilateral armoured exercise Bold Kurukshetra was reportedly held in India in 2025, with Singaporean armour training alongside Indian mechanised forces. The drill leverages India's ranges for Singapore's armour training.

    Exercise · 2024-25

    Surya Kiran 2024: India-Nepal drill

    The 18th India-Nepal Army exercise Surya Kiran was held in Nepal in late 2024–early 2025, focused on counter-terrorism in mountainous terrain. The battalion-level drill is the oldest continuous exercise with Nepal, reflecting the unique military relationship.

    Exercise · Oct 2024

    Sampriti 2024: India-Bangladesh Army drill

    The 11th India-Bangladesh Army exercise Sampriti was held in Meghalaya in October 2024, focused on counter-terrorism in semi-urban terrain. The drill is a barometer of the defence relationship that continued through Bangladesh's 2024 political transition.

    Exercise · 2024

    Jimex 2024: India-Japan naval drill

    The 8th Japan-India Maritime Exercise (JIMEX) was held off Japan in 2024, with destroyers, frigates and P-8Is conducting anti-submarine warfare drills. JIMEX complements the Quad's Malabar in binding the two navies.

    Exercise · 2024

    SITMEX 2024: India-Singapore-Thailand drill

    The trilateral SITMEX naval exercise with Singapore and Thailand was held in the Andaman Sea in 2024. The drill guards the Malacca Strait approaches — the jugular of Indo-Pacific trade — with coordinated anti-piracy serials.

    Exercise · 2025 · reported

    Cope India 2025? IAF's bilateral calendar (reported)

    The IAF's bilateral air exercises with the US (Cope India), France (Garuda) and others continued through 2024–25 on rotation, with Tarang Shakti 2024 as the multilateral flagship. The next Garuda edition with France is awaited (reported).

    Exercise · 2025 · reported

    Yudh Abhyas 2025: Alaska edition (reported)

    The 21st India-US Yudh Abhyas was reportedly held in Alaska in 2025, shifting to high-altitude and Arctic warfare scenarios. The rotation of venues — Rajasthan 2024, Alaska 2025 — tests both armies across extreme environments.

    Exercise · 2025 · reported

    Malabar 2025 in the Pacific (reported)

    The 29th Malabar exercise with the Quad navies was reportedly held in the Pacific in late 2025, continuing the high-end anti-submarine and air-defence serials. The exercise remains the Quad's most concrete military manifestation.

    Exercise · 2025 · reported

    Konkan 2025: India-UK naval drill (reported)

    The bilateral naval exercise Konkan with the Royal Navy was reportedly held in 2025, covering anti-submarine warfare and carrier operations. The drill supports the India-UK 2030 roadmap's defence pillar.

    Exercise · 1993-2026

    Varuna's growing complexity

    From its 1993 origins, the India-France Varuna naval exercise grew into a carrier-group-level drill by 2025, with Charles de Gaulle and Vikrant operating together. The 2026 edition at Toulon featured the upgraded, BrahMos-armed INS Trishul.

    Awards · Aug 2025

    Gallantry awards: 2025 Independence Day list

    The 2025 Independence Day gallantry list decorated Operation Sindoor's commanders and counter-terror heroes across J&K, with Kirti Chakras, Shaurya Chakras and Sena Medals announced. The Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal for Air Marshal Mishra headlined the wartime distinguished-service awards.

    National · Jan 2025 · reported

    Republic Day 2025: veterans' tableau

    The 76th Republic Day parade featured a veterans' tableau honouring 1971 war heroes alongside marching contingents of the new Agniveer intake — a symbolic passing of the baton. The flypast included Rafales in 'Sindoor' formation? No — the 2025 parade preceded the operation; the 2026 parade is expected to honour it (reported).

    Navy · 2025

    Navy's Information Fusion Centre grows

    The Information Fusion Centre–Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR) at Gurugram, the Navy's maritime-domain-awareness hub, expanded its international liaison network through 2024–25, now hosting officers from 12+ partner navies. White-shipping data sharing underpins anti-piracy and HADR responses.

    Reforms · 2024-26 · reported

    Andaman & Nicobar: tri-service hub strengthens

    India's only tri-service theatre command at Port Blair gained new surveillance, missile and air-defence assets through 2024–26 (reported), tightening the Malacca Strait watch. The command is the template for the planned mainland theatre commands.

    Missiles · 2024-25 · reported

    DRDO's 2024–25 test calendar

    Beyond the headline tests, DRDO's 2024–25 calendar included Astra Mk-II trials, Akash-NG user evaluations, extended-range Pinaka tests and the SMART torpedo-delivery system — a pipeline feeding the services' precision-strike transformation (reported).

    Army · 2025-26

    Army's drone doctrine takes shape

    Post-Sindoor, the Army formalised drone employment down to battalion level: Ashni drone platoons for surveillance-strike, loitering munitions for artillery spotting, and counter-drone guns for air defence. The 'Eagle on the Arm' goal makes every soldier drone-literate.

    Navy · 2025-26

    Make in India: 75% indigenous warships

    The Project 17A frigates commissioned in 2025–26 — Nilgiri, Udaygiri, Himgiri, Taragiri, Dunagiri — each carry about 75% indigenous content, built by Indian yards with 200+ MSME suppliers. The programme is the flagship proof of defence self-reliance.

    Industry · 2025

    Defence corridors: UP and Tamil Nadu

    The Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu defence industrial corridors attracted 100+ investment proposals by 2025, with BrahMos Aerospace's Lucknow unit and Tata-Airbus's Vadodara-adjacent ecosystem as anchors. The corridors aim to localise the supply chains behind the big 2025 deals.

    Defence · 2024-25

    Sainik Schools expansion: 100 new schools

    The 100 new Sainik Schools in partnership mode approved by the government continued rolling out through 2024–25, supplementing the 33 legacy schools. The expansion widens the NDA feeder pipeline beyond the traditional catchment states.

    Defence GK · 2025 · reported

    RIMC and RMS: the officer pipeline

    The Rashtriya Indian Military College (1922) and the five Rashtriya Military Schools remained the premier feeder institutions for the NDA through 2025, with record applications reported. Their alumni include service chiefs across generations.

    Coast Guard · 2025

    Coast Guard's expanding fleet (2025)

    The Indian Coast Guard — the fourth armed force under the Defence Ministry — continued its fleet expansion through 2025 with new offshore patrol vessels and pollution-control ships from Indian yards. It guards the 7,500-km coastline and 2.3 million sq km EEZ.

    Awards · 2025

    Param Vir Chakra: 21 heroes

    No new Param Vir Chakra has been awarded since the four Kargil heroes of 1999 — the tally stands at 21. Operation Sindoor's gallantry was recognised through the Yudh Seva and Sena Medal series instead, keeping the PVC's wartime-extraordinary bar intact.

    Awards GK

    Maha Vir Chakra's double heroes

    Wing Commander Jag Mohan Nath remains among the very few officers decorated with the Maha Vir Chakra twice (1962 and 1965). The MVC is India's second-highest wartime gallantry award, after the Param Vir Chakra.

    Defence GK

    UN peacekeeping: India's enduring role

    Through 2024–26 India remained among the largest uniformed contributors to UN peacekeeping, with infantry battalions, engineers and the legacy of the first all-women police unit (Liberia, 2007). Captain Salaria's 1961 Congo PVC remains the mission's iconic Indian sacrifice.

    Welfare · 2025-26

    Veterans: OROP and ex-servicemen welfare

    One Rank One Pension arrears disbursal and the Agniveer Seva Nidhi package stayed in focus through 2025–26, alongside expanded ECHS healthcare for veterans. Welfare of the 30-lakh-strong veteran community is a standing CDS-level priority.

    Outlook · 2026

    The road ahead: 2026–27 outlook

    With the CDS and Army Chief transitions complete by mid-2026, the forces entered 2026–27 focused on theatre-command rollout, the AMCA and Project 75I decisions, and sustaining the post-Sindoor operational tempo. The 'new normal' doctrine now frames every procurement and deployment choice.

    Defence · Sep 2026

    Tarang Shakti 2026 begins (26 September 2026)

    The second edition of the IAF-hosted multinational air exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 started at Jodhpur on 26 September 2026 (runs till 12 October). For the first time, the IAF is exercising with the US F-35 stealth fighter (2–3 jets); France sent Rafales, the UAE F-16s, and Bangladesh a C-130J.

    Defence · Sep 2026

    Veer Guardian-2026: Japanese fighters fly from Indian soil (20 September 2026)

    The India–Japan bilateral air exercise Veer Guardian-2026 (9–22 September, Jodhpur) saw Japanese F-2A fighters operate from Indian soil for the first time. On 20 September, IAF chief AP Singh and JASDF chief Gen Takehiro Morita flew a Tejas formation sortie and exchanged badges.

    Defence · Sep 2026

    Bay of Bengal missile-test NOTAM (25–26 September 2026)

    India notified an almost 600 km danger zone in the Bay of Bengal for a missile test on 25–26 September 2026, the second such notification after May. The missile type was undisclosed — analysts speculated Pralay, a Prithvi-series missile, or an extended-range BrahMos — with Kalam Island, Odisha, the likely launch base.

    Defence · Sep 2026

    KAL drone tested at Pokhran (21 September 2026)

    IG Defence of Noida flight-tested the KAL at Pokhran on 21 September 2026 — India’s first indigenous long-range (about 1,000 km) one-way attack drone. The vehicle-launched kamikaze UAV was first disclosed in March 2026 and shown at the North Tech Symposium, Prayagraj.

    Defence · Sep 2026

    CDS 2 and NDA 2 2026 exams held (13 September 2026)

    UPSC conducted the Combined Defence Services (II) and NDA/NA (II) 2026 written examinations on 13 September 2026, in pen-and-paper mode. CDS 2 advertised 451 vacancies and NDA 2 advertised 394 posts; the application window had closed on 9 June 2026.

    Defence · Sep 2026

    NDTV Defence Summit 2026: ‘future-ready’ strategy (27 September 2026)

    Defence Minister Rajnath Singh told the NDTV Defence Summit on 27 September 2026 that India’s defence strategy is ‘future-ready’ for the 5th generation of multi-domain warfare — ‘if you want peace, prepare for war’ — and that Indian defence products now reach over 100 countries: ‘Made in India’ is ‘Trust in India’.

    Air exercise · Sep 2026

    Veer Guardian 2026 concludes (22 September 2026)

    The bilateral air exercise between the Indian Air Force and the Japan Air Self-Defence Force concluded at Air Force Station Jodhpur on 22 September 2026 after 14 days of joint flying. The IAF fielded Su-30 MKI, Rafale and the indigenous Tejas, while the JASDF flew Mitsubishi F-2A fighters — the first-ever visit of Japanese fighter aircraft to India. On Distinguished Visitors’ Day both air chiefs, Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh and General Takehiro Morita, flew the Tejas. The Ministry of Defence called the second edition a milestone for the India–Japan defence partnership.

    Acquisition · Sep 2026

    MoD signs Rs 811-crore SAT-SAAW deal with BDL (23 September 2026)

    The Ministry of Defence signed a Rs 811-crore contract with Bharat Dynamics Ltd on 23 September 2026 for 160 satellite-guided smart anti-airfield weapons (SAT-SAAW) for the Indian Air Force. The DRDO-developed precision-guided glide bomb has a declared range of up to 100 km and accuracy under seven metres with INS-GPS guidance (under three metres with a seeker). It will arm the Jaguar, Hawk and Su-30MKI fleets — integration on Rafale and Tejas Mk1A is also planned — and was combat-tested against Pakistani airfields during Operation Sindoor. The weapon carries 60% indigenous content.

    Army exercise · Sep 2026

    Yudh Abhyas 2026 live-fire at Mahajan (24 September 2026)

    The US and Indian armies completed a bilateral live-fire exercise at the Mahajan Field Firing Range, Rajasthan, on 24 September 2026 during Yudh Abhyas 2026, integrating artillery, air defence, counter-UAS and aviation. India fielded the Pinaka multi-barrel rocket launcher, M777 ultra-light howitzer, Dhanush artillery system, L70 air-defence guns, Swathi weapon-locating radar and AH-64E Apache attack helicopters; the US Army fielded HIMARS and the M-LIDS counter-drone system. US Ambassador Sergio Gor and Lt Gen Vikrant Suresh Deshpande (GOC, 10 Corps) watched the demonstration. The 22nd edition is being held simultaneously at Mahajan and Auli, Uttarakhand, with about 600 personnel from each side.

    Defence exports · Sep 2026

    Defence exports target: Rs 50,000 crore in two years (25 September 2026)

    Speaking at the 13th PAFI Annual Forum on 25 September 2026, Defence Secretary Rajesh Singh said India’s defence exports should reach Rs 50,000 crore within two years, up from Rs 38,424 crore in 2025–26. He said India’s cost edge is a key USP — Indian missiles can be offered at almost one-fourth of foreign OEM prices — and named BrahMos, artillery and mounted gun systems, DRDO-technology private-sector products and the Akash surface-to-air missile as export draws. The defence exporter base has expanded to 145 firms.

    Maritime · Sep 2026

    ICG ship Shaunak sails for Perth on QUAD-at-Sea mission (25 September 2026)

    Indian Coast Guard ship Shaunak sailed from Chennai on 25 September 2026 for Perth, Australia, as part of the QUAD-at-Sea Ship Observer Mission with six ‘Sea Riders’ embarked — two officers each from India and Japan and one each from Australia and the United States. The mission builds maritime interoperability and professional exchanges among the four Quad countries, aligned with the Quad Foreign Ministers’ joint statement of 26 May 2026 and India’s MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) vision for the Indo-Pacific.

    Border security · Sep 2026

    COAS reviews Chinar Corps readiness along LoC (25 September 2026)

    Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth visited forward areas and formations of the Chinar Corps under Northern Command on 25 September 2026 to review operational preparedness along the Line of Control and counter-terrorist operations in the hinterland. He commended all ranks for their vigilance and reiterated the ‘VIJAY’ five-point framework for a future-ready Army. At Tangdhar he visited the Operation Drishti 2026 advanced surgical eye camp (23–30 September), where specialist teams from Army Hospital (R&R) and 92 Base Hospital are screening over 6,000 patients and planning more than 400 eye surgeries.

    Air exercise · Sep 2026

    Tarang Shakti 2026: F-35 debuts over India (28 September 2026)

    The Indian Air Force commenced the operational phase of Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 at Air Force Station Jodhpur on 28 September 2026. Running from 26 September to 12 October under the theme ‘Power in Partnership’, the multilateral exercise has seven friendly foreign countries participating — the United States, France, Australia, UAE, Germany, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh — with the US F-35 Lightning II, French Rafale, F-16, A400M, MRTT, C-130J and KC-30A among the foreign aircraft. It is the first time an F-35 has taken part in an IAF exercise on Indian soil; about 32 countries are attending as observers. The second edition builds on the inaugural 2024 exercise.

    Army exercise · Sep 2026

    KAZIND-2026 begins in Kazakhstan (28 September 2026)

    A 60-member Indian Armed Forces contingent departed for Oskemen, Kazakhstan, on 28 September 2026 for the ninth edition of the India–Kazakhstan joint military exercise KAZIND-2026, scheduled till 11 October. The Indian side is drawn mainly from a battalion of the Garhwal Rifles along with personnel from other arms and services and the Indian Air Force; Kazakhstan fields a matching contingent from its Land Forces. The exercise focuses on joint counter-terrorism operations in semi-urban and mountainous terrain under a UN mandate, with emphasis on air mobility, UAS and counter-UAS capabilities, joint command posts and a final validation exercise.

    12-week battle plan

    Six study days, one test-and-review day. Repeat weak topics, not familiar ones.

    Weeks 1–4

    Build the base

    • 90 min core subject
    • 45 min English / reasoning
    • 30 min GK revision
    • 20 min running + mobility
    • One sectional test weekly
    Weeks 5–8

    Increase pressure

    • Mixed timed sets
    • Error notebook by topic
    • Two full sections weekly
    • One PPDT story + narration
    • Progressive run intervals
    Weeks 9–12

    Simulate selection

    • Two full mocks weekly
    • OMR / CBT discipline
    • Revise only marked gaps
    • Interview speaking drills
    • Taper before exam day
    Rule

    Every wrong answer must become one line in an error log: concept missed → why I chose it → rule that fixes it. Reattempt those questions after 48 hours and again after one week.

It is being held for the first time in a two-theatre format: a desert and precision-fires phase at the Mahajan Field Firing Ranges in Rajasthan, followed by a high-altitude phase at Auli in Uttarakhand.
