    Defence Secretary's Armenia visit: MoU on defence R&D (17 Aug)

    Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh visited Yerevan on 16–17 August 2026 and signed an MoU on cooperation in research, development, innovation and shared production in the defence industry. He met Armenia's High Tech Industry Minister Davit Tadevosyan, Defence Minister Suren Papikyan and Chief of General Staff Lt Gen Edvard Asryan.

    Diplomacy · Aug 2026

    India-Armenia: Joint Services Staff Talks institutionalised

    During the Defence Secretary's August 2026 visit, India and Armenia exchanged the Terms of Reference for institutionalising Joint Services Staff Talks between the two armed forces. The MoD noted Armenia is diversifying defence procurement with India emerging as a major partner.

    Leadership · Jul 2026

    New Vice Chiefs take charge (1 Jul)

    Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit took over as Vice Chief of the Air Staff and Lt Gen Sandeep Jain as Vice Chief of the Army Staff on 1 July 2026. Dixit, an experimental test pilot with 3,500+ flying hours, was Chief of Integrated Defence Staff during Operation Sindoor; Jain, of the Mahar Regiment, was Southern Army Commander.

    Leadership · Jul 2026

    New Army Commanders and CISC

    In the July 2026 reshuffle, Lt Gen Rajesh Pushkar took over the Southern Command and Lt Gen Mohit Malhotra the Jaipur-based South Western Command, while Air Marshal Tejinder Singh became Chief of Integrated Defence Staff.

    IAF · Sep 2026

    Tejas Mk1A deliveries to begin Aug–Sep 2026

    HAL Chairman and Managing Director Ravi Kota said Tejas Mk1A deliveries to the IAF will start by August–September 2026 as the GE F404 engine supply stabilises. Engine delays from the US had held up the programme; HAL has invoked liquidated damages on GE under the contract.

    IAF · Sep 2026

    Three more F404 engines reach HAL (Aug 2026)

    GE Aerospace shipped three more F404-IN20 engines to HAL in August 2026, taking total deliveries to 10 under the Rs 5,375-crore contract for 99 engines signed in 2021. The IAF has ordered 180 Tejas Mk1A aircraft in total.

    IAF · Sep 2026

    30 Tejas Mk1A airframes ready, awaiting engines

    About 30 Tejas Mk1A aircraft have been manufactured, flown and tested by HAL and are awaiting combat-ready engines for formal induction. HAL is targeting the handover of up to 24 jets to the IAF by the end of the year.

    IAF · Sep 2026

    MRFA: Letter of Request for 114 Rafales finalised (May 2026)

    India finalised the Letter of Request for 114 Rafale fighter jets under the Multi-Role Fighter Aircraft programme in May 2026, with France expected to respond by mid-August. Around 90–94 of the jets are to be manufactured in India with Dassault, taking indigenous content toward 50–60 per cent.

    Army · Sep 2026

    Bhairav battalions: 5 raised, 25 more in six months

    Director General Infantry Lt Gen Ajay Kumar said five Bhairav light commando battalions have been raised, with 25 more to follow within six months. Each ~250-strong battalion bridges the gap between conventional infantry and Special Forces for swift strikes along the borders.

    Army · Jul 2025

    Bhairav battalions announced at Dras

    Then-COAS General Upendra Dwivedi announced the raising of Bhairav light commando battalions on 26 July 2025 during the Kargil Vijay Diwas commemorations at Dras. The lean, tech-enabled units carry Javelin anti-tank missiles, AK-203 rifles and armed drones.

    Army · Sep 2026

    Ashni drone platoon for every infantry battalion

    Each of the Army's ~380 infantry battalions is raising an Ashni drone platoon with about 10 drones — four for surveillance and six combat types including loitering munitions and kamikaze drones. The "eagle on the arm" concept aims for 100 per cent drone literacy among soldiers.

    Reforms · Sep 2026

    MoD Annual Report 2025-26: post-Sindoor drone push

    The MoD Annual Report 2025-26 says Operation Sindoor's lessons drove a war-footing induction of unmanned aerial systems, counter-UAS, loitering munitions, air defence and electronic warfare. It candidly notes indigenous industry's inability so far to offer niche products in the UAS and loitering-munition domains.

    Reforms · Sep 2026

    Nine fast-track drone projects under ADITI/DISC

    To close the drone gap flagged after Operation Sindoor, the Army moved nine Fast Track Development Projects under ADITI and DISC, endorsed by the Defence Secretary for iDEX execution. A Core Committee on UAS and C-UAS now decides inductions, and a dedicated Special Purpose Vehicle with special financial powers is proposed.

    Reforms · Sep 2026

    Rudra Brigades, Shaktibaan, Divyastra, Bhairav introduced

    The MoD Annual Report 2025-26 lists the new formations introduced under force restructuring: Rudra Brigades, Shaktibaan Regiments, Divyastra Batteries and Bhairav Battalions. Orders have been issued for 15 Bhairav Battalions for hybrid warfare and high-tempo operations.

    Army · Sep 2026

    Rs 2,770-crore carbine deal: 4.2 lakh CQB carbines

    The Army signed a Rs 2,770-crore contract for 4.2 lakh close-quarter battle carbines — 60 per cent to be made by Bharat Forge and the rest by PLR Systems, the Adani Defence–Israel Weapon Industries joint venture. Deliveries start within a year.

    Army · Sep 2026

    Emergency Javelin buy from the US

    To cover the shortage of new-generation man-portable anti-tank guided missiles, India is making an emergency procurement of 12 Javelin launchers and 104 missiles from the United States until an indigenous option is viable.

    Army · Sep 2026

    "Shoot-to-kill": 7.62mm upgrade across infantry

    The infantry's shift from a "shoot-to-wound" to "shoot-to-kill" philosophy has driven the upgrade of assault rifles and light machine guns from 5.56mm to 7.62mm calibre, with vintage sniper rifles being replaced by .338-calibre weapons.

    Army · Sep 2026

    Foliage-penetration radar, new ATGM in the pipeline

    The Army is processing cases for an anti-tank guided missile system and a foliage-penetration radar, DG Infantry Lt Gen Ajay Kumar said. The radar, paired with a drone proven in recent operations, has demonstrated significant operational value.

    IAF · Sep 2026

    Squadron strength down to ~30 against 42.5 sanctioned

    The IAF is operating around 30 fighter squadrons against a sanctioned 42.5, with MiG retirements and Tejas delays widening the gap. The IAF has acquired retired Jaguar airframes from the UK to cannibalise for spares and keep the fleet flying.

    Navy · Apr 2026

    INS Aridhaman commissioned (3 Apr 2026)

    Defence Minister Rajnath Singh commissioned INS Aridhaman, India's third nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine, at Visakhapatnam on 3 April 2026. The S4 boat is the third of the Arihant class, giving the Navy three operational SSBNs for the first time.

    Navy · Apr 2026

    Aridhaman: 7,000 tonnes, 8 missile tubes

    INS Aridhaman displaces about 7,000 tonnes — larger than the 6,000-tonne Arihant and Arighaat — and doubles the missile payload with 8 launch tubes for up to 24 K-15 Sagarika or 8 K-4 missiles. The K-4's ~3,500-km range enables strikes deep into adversary territory from Indian waters.

    Exam · Sep 2026

    NDA & NA (II) 2026 held on 13 September

    The UPSC conducted the National Defence Academy and Naval Academy Examination (II) 2026 on 13 September 2026. The Combined Defence Services (II) 2026 examination was held the same day.

    Exam · Sep 2026

    AFCAT 2 2026 results declared (9 Sep)

    The Indian Air Force declared the AFCAT 2 2026 results on 9 September 2026 for 379 vacancies across flying and ground-duty branches. It remains the principal officer-entry gateway for graduates outside the NDA/CDS route.

    UN · Sep 2026

    Australia launches UNSC 2029-30 bid (21 Sep)

    Prime Minister Anthony Albanese launched Australia's campaign for a non-permanent UN Security Council seat for the 2029-30 term on 21 September in New York. Australia faces Finland for the Western European and Others Group seat; the election by secret ballot is expected in 2028.

    IAF · Oct 2026

    Air Force Day observed (8 Oct)

    The Indian Air Force observes its 94th anniversary on 8 October 2026, weeks after the F-35's landmark appearance at Tarang Shakti and amid the Tejas Mk1A delivery restart and the 114-Rafale MRFA process.

    Army · Oct 2026

    Shaurya Diwas: Infantry Day on 27 October

    The Army observes Shaurya Diwas (Infantry Day) on 27 October, marking the 1947 airlift of Indian troops to Srinagar. DG Infantry's 2026 announcements — Bhairav battalions and Ashni drone platoons — headline this year's modernisation theme.

    Army · Nov 2026

    First Bhairav battalion to be fully operational (1 Nov)

    The Army's first Bhairav light commando battalion is set to be fully operationalised on 1 November 2026 after on-the-job training, with four more battalions under raising and 25 planned within six months.

    Exercise · Oct 2026

    Tarang Shakti 2026 concludes (12 Oct)

    The IAF's Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 concludes on 12 October at Jodhpur after over two weeks of multinational air combat training — the edition remembered for the F-35's first tactical participation in an Indian-hosted drill.

    Exercise · Oct 2026

    Nomadic Elephant 2026 concludes (3 Oct)

    The 18th India-Mongolia Exercise Nomadic Elephant concludes on 3 October at Pithoragarh, wrapping up two weeks of joint counter-insurgency training in semi-urban and mountainous terrain.

    Diplomacy · Sep 2026

    Australia's UNSC bid: India watches the contest

    With Australia and Finland contesting the 2029-30 Western European and Others Group seat, the 2028 secret-ballot election is one to track. India, a long-standing advocate of Security Council reform, follows every UNSC candidature as part of its multilateral positioning.

    Defence · Sep 2026

    "Eagle on the arm": every soldier a drone operator

    The Army's "eagle on the arm" concept aims to make every soldier drone-literate, with Ashni platoons organic to all ~380 infantry battalions. Nine drone types are under trial evaluation for ISR and strike roles alongside the deals already inked.

    Defence · Sep 2026

    Defence exports: 145 exporters, 80+ countries

    The FY2025-26 export record of Rs 38,424 crore came from 145 Indian exporters supplying more than 80 countries, with BrahMos, Pinaka, radars and patrol vessels leading. DPSUs and private firms both contributed to the 62.66 per cent jump.

    Defence · Sep 2026

    Atmanirbhar September: DAC, APUs and exports

    September 2026 summed up the Atmanirbhar push: Rs 1.10 lakh crore of DAC approvals with 98 per cent Indian sourcing, a Rs 586-crore Make-II tank APU contract, and record FY2025-26 exports of Rs 38,424 crore. Procurement, production and exports moved in lockstep.

    Leadership · Jul 2026

    Dixit: test pilot to VCAS

    New Vice Chief of the Air Staff Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit is an experimental test pilot and qualified flying instructor with experience on Mirage-2000, MiG variants, Jaguar, Tejas and Hawk. Commissioned on 6 December 1986, he flew in Op Safed Sagar, Op Rakshak and Op Sindoor.

    Leadership · Jul 2026

    Jain: Mahar Regiment to VCOAS

    New Vice Chief of the Army Staff Lt Gen Sandeep Jain was commissioned into the Mahar Regiment in June 1988. He has served in Operation Pawan in Sri Lanka, UN Mission in South Sudan, and multiple counter-insurgency tenures along the LoC and in the North East.

    Defence · Sep 2026

    September 2026: the busiest defence month

    September 2026 packed a DAC mega-approval, the APU contract, Tarang Shakti with the F-35, Yudh Abhyas in two theatres, Nomadic Elephant with Mongolia, record export figures and new Vice Chiefs — the densest single month of defence current affairs in the 2025-26 cycle.

    Indigenisation

    DRDO IRSA 2.0; new IAF software-defined radio by year-end (29 September 2026)

    29 Sep 2026 — DRDO has notified IRSA 2.0, the upgraded Indian Radio Software Architecture standard for military software-defined radios, developed by its Defence Electronics Applications Laboratory (DEAL). The IAF's new indigenous SDR built on the standard is expected by end-2026, joining the Navy's existing IRSA-based sets. Why it matters: a common waveform standard lets Army, Navy and IAF radios interoperate securely.

    Defence Industry

    Paras Defence wins Rs 26.59 cr DRDO hyperspectral order (29 September 2026)

    29 Sep 2026 — Paras Defence and Space Technologies has won a Rs 26.59-crore DRDO order as Lead System Integrator for the optics and opto-mechanical unit of a hyperspectral mission — a space-borne payload for Earth observation, deliverable by 27 September 2027. The domestic order spotlights private industry's growing role in strategic space payloads.

    Neighbourhood Watch

    Pakistan's Hangor submarine: maiden live missile firing (29 September 2026)

    29 Sep 2026 — Pakistan's newly inducted Hangor-class submarine conducted its maiden live missile firing on 27 September 2026, according to ISPR. The Hangor class is being built with Chinese collaboration under the 2015 deal for eight submarines. For CDS/AFCAT: track how Pakistan's sea-denial build-up shapes India's anti-submarine warfare priorities.

    Navy

    Navy Commanders' Conference, 29 Sep–1 Oct (29 September 2026)

    29 Sep 2026 — The Navy's second biannual Commanders' Conference of 2026 opens on 29 September at Nausena Bhawan, New Delhi, running till 1 October. Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh addresses the opening day; the CDS and Army Chief join for tri-services synergy. Top of the agenda: Operation Urja Suraksha — the Navy's mission guarding energy shipments through the Strait of Hormuz since March 2026.

    Defence Policy

    Rajnath: future-ready for 5th-generation warfare (29 September 2026)

    29 Sep 2026 — Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said on 27 September 2026 that India's armed forces must be future-ready for fifth-generation warfare spanning cyber, space, information and autonomous systems alongside conventional domains. The remark frames the ongoing push for integrated theatre commands, indigenous SDRs like IRSA 2.0, and AI-enabled warfighting.

    Navy

    Rajnath: 2026 "historic year" for Navy — 18 warships (29 September 2026)

    29 Sep 2026 — Addressing the Naval Commanders' Conference on 29 September 2026, Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh said 2026 would be a historic year for the Indian Navy, with 18 warships slated for induction or commissioning — the largest single-year force accretion in its history. He noted that recently commissioned warships carry over 75% indigenous content and urged the Navy to export warships to friendly foreign nations. For CDS/AFCAT: the conference is the Navy's apex-level biannual meet, held this time from 29 September to 1 October at Nausena Bhawan, New Delhi.

    Navy

    Navy takes command of CTF-154; Operation Southern Readiness at Kochi (29 September 2026)

    29 Sep 2026 — The Indian Navy assumed command of Combined Task Force-154 under the Combined Maritime Forces, and during its tenure conducted Operation Southern Readiness at Kochi with 276 personnel from 27 countries, 76 facilitators and subject-matter experts, and four international organisations. CTF-154 is the CMF task force focused on maritime security training and capacity building. For CDS/AFCAT: the CMF is a multinational naval partnership headquartered in Bahrain.

    Navy

    INS Sudarshini's Lokayan-26: maritime diplomacy across the Atlantic (29 September 2026)

    29 Sep 2026 — The Navy's sail training ship INS Sudarshini undertook the Lokayan-26 deployment across the United States, the Atlantic and the Mediterranean, strengthening maritime diplomacy and engagement with the Indian diaspora while showcasing India's maritime heritage. For CDS/AFCAT: Sudarshini and INS Tarangini are the Navy's two sail training ships; such voyages build seamanship in officer cadets.

    Navy

    "All Ranks, All Roles": women officers on frontline warships (29 September 2026)

    29 Sep 2026 — Rajnath Singh commended the Navy's "All Ranks, All Roles" approach at the Commanders' Conference, highlighting the deployment of women officers on frontline warships and aircraft and their participation in naval navigational expeditions, including the Navika Sagar Parikrama circumnavigation voyage. For CDS/AFCAT: Navika Sagar Parikrama is the Indian Navy's all-women circumnavigation expedition.

    Defence Policy

    "First responder and preferred security partner": Rajnath on India's IOR role (29 September 2026)

    29 Sep 2026 — Addressing the Naval Commanders' Conference, Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh said India stands as a first responder and preferred security partner in the Indian Ocean Region, adding: "If the seas are secure, India will be secure; and if India is secure, the resolve for a Viksit Bharat will be further strengthened." He described the Navy as a strategic anchor in the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision.

    Diagnostic test

    Spotted a mistake in a question? Report it here — corrections go live in the next daily refresh.

    15 mixed questions. One point each. No penalty here—use the explanations to find your weakest area.

    —/15

    Answer every question, then submit. Your result stays only for this visit.

    SSB practice room

    SSB is not a personality costume. Practise clear observation, usable ideas, teamwork and honest reflection.

    PPDT in 4 minutes

    Observe for 30 seconds. Note characters, mood and action. Write a realistic story with a clear protagonist, practical plan, teamwork and measurable outcome. Then narrate in under one minute.

    TAT story frame

    Situation → goal → obstacles → organised action → result. Avoid miracles, melodrama and unsupported heroics. Show initiative without making everyone else passive.

    WAT response

    Write the first constructive, grammatically complete thought. Do not force moral slogans. “Risk” could become: “Calculated risk follows preparation and backup planning.”

    Interview ledger

    Prepare truthful examples for responsibility, conflict, failure, improvement, teamwork and decision-making. Know your education, family context, hobbies and reasons for choosing the service.

    Group discussion: a useful speaking pattern

    Enter with one grounded point, add evidence or an example, connect to another candidate’s useful idea, and invite the group toward a conclusion. Volume is not leadership.

    Lecturette: 3-minute structure

    Open with a definition and relevance. Use three ordered points, one example, one counterpoint and a brief conclusion. Practise with a timer; do not memorise ornate openings.

    What not to manufacture

    Do not invent achievements, rehearse a false “ideal officer” persona or hide obvious weaknesses behind clichés. Consistency across psychological tests, interview and group tasks matters.

    Physical readiness

    Train above the minimum gradually. Official standards differ by entry, category and notification.

    Starter week × 4

    1. Mon: easy 20–30 min run + mobility
    2. Tue: push-ups, squats, rows, plank—3 rounds
    3. Wed: 6 × 200 m controlled intervals
    4. Thu: walk, stretch, sleep focus
    5. Fri: tempo run + core
    6. Sat: timed 1.6 km every second week
    7. Sun: full recovery

    Progress without injury

    Increase weekly running volume by no more than roughly 10% when your body is adapting well. Use shoes that fit, warm up before fast work, and keep at least one recovery day.

    Stop and seek qualified medical advice for chest pain, fainting, severe breathlessness, or persistent bone/joint pain. Medical eligibility is decided by the relevant service—not by this guide.
